extracted.intended_audience: professional astronomers and spectroscopists; readers interested in solar observations and theory
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical criteria for observing, classifying, and interpreting the forms and spectra of solar protuberances to infer whether they are eruptive jets or chromospheric alterations. Emphasises multi-station contemporaneous observation, instrumentation effects, morphological classification, spectral composition, and statistical sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish the general character of protuberances
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether protuberances are true eruptive jets (narrow at base, spreading out like a fan) or broad-based structures tapering upwards like a pyramid, since this distinction bears on whether the subjacent strata of the sun are solid, liquid, or gaseous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tacchini emphasises that resolving this basic morphological character is of great importance and is the primary question to be settled to distinguish eruption-driven phenomena from chromospheric alterations. Use morphological statistics and complementary spectral evidence to support conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use contemporaneous multi-station observations to avoid certain sources of error
rubrics_metrics.description: Make observations at multiple geographically separated stations at the same times (e.g., Palermo, Rome, Padua) to ensure the objects seen are identical and to remove doubts about instrumental or local seeing effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tacchini invited collaborators to observe from 1–13 July, 1871, from 7–10 o'clock, finding principal characters identical across stations. Contemporaneous observation reduces misinterpretation arising from rapid changes or local seeing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare results across different instruments and drawing methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for differences introduced by the spectroscope/telescope type (direct-vision prisms vs angular-vision instruments) and by modes of drawing; these can produce systematic differences in delineations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge that differences between Rome and Palermo arose from mode of drawing and greater distinctness of vision at Palermo; large instruments give more detail than small ones. Cross-compare instruments to distinguish real phenomena from instrument-dependent artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphological classification: jets (fan/tree-like) versus broad-based (pyramidal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify protuberances into forms: (a) narrow at base and spreading (tree/fan-like, suggestive of volcanic-type eruptions) and (b) broad base tapering upwards like a pyramid (suggestive of chromospheric throwing up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tacchini's dataset: out of 2,903 protuberances only 234 (~8%) have the tree/fan form, while ~92% have broad base/pyramidal form. Use these proportions when arguing for the dominant mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify frequencies/statistics of observed forms and spectra
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect large samples and report proportions of morphological and spectral types (e.g., percent tree-like, percent with mixed spectra).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tacchini reports 2,903 protuberances observed; ~8% tree-like; about 10 out of 100 give a mixed spectrum while ~90 give spectra showing only hydrogen-lines and the D line. Robust statistical sampling is necessary to infer the general nature of protuberances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure heights and check consistency across methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure protuberance heights and compare values obtained by different observational/measurement methods to test reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tacchini notes that heights are for the most part the same across diverse methods, which supports the reality of measured heights despite method diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise and separate sources of observational differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish differences due to rapid real changes in protuberances from differences due to drawing technique or superior vision at one site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tacchini identifies two kinds of differences between sets of delineations: those arising from mode of drawing and those from greater distinctness of vision; other differences may be real (rapid changes). Explicitly document observing/drawing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyse spectral composition for mixed versus simple spectra
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether protuberances exhibit mixed spectra (many bright lines corresponding to various elements) or simple spectra (hydrogen lines and the D line alone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If protuberances were produced by violent eruptions from the solar interior, many elements should be present throughout the height of the protuberance. Tacchini finds that mixed composition is usually limited to a small height (the base) and that the higher portions are composed exclusively of hydrogen and the element D; in his sample only ~10% show mixed spectra beyond the base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess vertical distribution of chemical constituents within protuberances
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine whether elements other than hydrogen occur throughout the protuberance or are confined to the base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tacchini's observations indicate varied composition is limited to the mere base of the protuberance while higher portions show only hydrogen and D; this spatial confinement argues against deep eruptions ejecting heavy elements to great heights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use spectral evidence to test eruption hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the presence, absence, and vertical distribution of bright spectral lines (magnesium, iron, sodium, titanium, calcium, barium, nickel, chromium, copper, etc., plus hydrogen and Helium/‘Helium-like’ element) to infer whether material is ejected from interior or originates in the chromosphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tacchini argues that if eruptive, the varied substances ejected would attain considerable height and be detectable throughout, but observation shows mixed lines chiefly at the base and hydrogen/D high up — thus weighing against a solid-crust eruption model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider alternative mechanisms such as descent (solar rain) forming protuberances
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate hypotheses in which protuberances arise from a descent of matter from above (a ‘solar rain’) where luminous hydrogen clouds throw off filaments that descend and unite at the solar limb to form protuberances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tacchini describes observations where jets have counterparts in descending matter; include this mechanism as a potential explanation and look for observational signatures (filaments descending on both sides and uniting at the sun’s edge).

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe chromosphere structure with high resolution to test continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use large instruments and favourable seeing to inspect the chromosphere for continuity versus a discontinuous series of flames; a continuous crust would present a level stratum, whereas distinct flames indicate an active, non-solid chromosphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tacchini notes that with large instruments the chromosphere often appears as a continuous series of distinct flames, resembling a general conflagration, which undermines the existence of a solid or pasty crust on the sun's surface. Document instrument aperture and seeing conditions when reporting such structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document exceptional cases and anomalous spectra carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Record and describe rare or exceptional protuberances (e.g., one case where hydrogen lines and D were accompanied by other bright lines at higher portions) since they may constrain models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tacchini reports a specific observation on December 19, 1871, of a magnificent protuberance whose central part exhibited two red lines; such exceptions should be logged in detail and compared with the statistical norm.
